title: Faster and more precise isotopic water analysis of discrete samples
author: Hachgenei, Vaury, et al.

steps.title: Prepare standards and samples
steps.instruction: Open the sealed glass ampoules of PICARRO ZERO, MID and DEPL on the day of analysis, transfer each to an analysis vial, and perform 12 high‑precision injections (8 min per injection) for each standard in the order: tap water, PICARRO DEPL, PICARRO MID, tap water, PICARRO ZERO.

steps.title: Check for memory‑effect trend
steps.instruction: Calculate the difference between the first and last injection values for each isotope; if the difference is ≤0.15 ‰ for δ¹⁸O or ≤0.4 ‰ for δ²H, skip fitting and use the classic averaging‑over‑last‑injections (aol) method.

steps.title: Fit linear inv function
steps.instruction: Fit the model y = a·x + b (y = measured isotope ratio, x = injection number) to the injection series using Python's scipy.optimize.curve_fit with sigma(x) = 11 + 0.5·x (giving a weight of 1 + 0.5·x for the x‑th injection). Optimize parameters a and b; if curve_fit raises a runtime error, revert to the aol method.

steps.title: Extract corrected measured value
steps.instruction: Take the fitted intercept b as the memory‑corrected measured isotope ratio for the sample (or standard).

steps.title: Calibrate each standard set
steps.instruction: For each set of standards (e.g., beginning and end of a run), apply steps 2‑4 to obtain measured values, then fit a linear calibration (real isotope value vs. measured value) to obtain slope and intercept, and record the central time of the set (midpoint between the first injection of the first standard and the last injection of the last standard).

steps.title: Interpolate calibration to samples
steps.instruction: For each sample, compute its central measurement time (midpoint between its first and last injection) and linearly interpolate the slope and intercept from the two neighboring standard‑set calibrations based on time.

steps.title: Apply calibration to sample
steps.instruction: Calculate the final isotopic ratio for the sample by applying the interpolated calibration: predicted value = (interpolated slope) × (b) + (interpolated intercept), where b is the corrected measured value from step 4.

steps.title: Recommended injection count and weighting
steps.instruction: Use at least six injections per sample (each injection ≈8 min). Weight later injections more heavily by using sigma(x)=11+0.5·x (or similar decreasing sigma such as sigma(x)=1·x or sigma(x)=exp(−0.2x), which does not materially affect results). If no trend is detected, average over the last injections (e.g., last 5, 4, 3, 2, or 1 injection depending on total number).
